SELECTED_INDEX: 6
CONFIDENCE: 0.31
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H stretching (strong 2941 cm⁻¹) plus two medium-intensity bands at 2794 and 2838 cm⁻¹. A well-known pair of Raman bands near 2790–2840 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the symmetric C–H stretches of N-methyl groups in a dimethyl-substituted tertiary amine; candidates 3, 6, 7 and 10 contain N(CH₃)₂ units, while 1 & 2 (simple ethers/alcohols) do not.  

Candidate 6 (CN(C)C(C)(C)CO) is the simplest molecule with an N(CH₃)₂ group and only aliphatic atoms, matching the very limited number of observed bands. Its tert-butyl skeleton can supply the CH₃/CH₂ rocking modes at 691 and 720 cm⁻¹, CH₃ deformations at 1450 cm⁻¹ and 1411 cm⁻¹, and a C–N / C–O stretch near 964 cm⁻¹. The low-frequency 578 cm⁻¹ band can arise from C–C–O skeletal bending in small alkanols. More complex sulfone or phosphate candidates would be expected to show strong S=O or P=O stretches (typically 1000–1350 cm⁻¹) that are absent here. Therefore candidate 6 best fits the experimental pattern.
